messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got back from the city — everything’s running as usual, maybe even smoother than before. Noticed a few quiet changes: permits are still stalled, but people are planting gardens and fixing up homes like they expect to stay. Seems like the calm’s deeper than it looks. Be careful what you say, even among trusted friends."
Sender 2: "The quiet’s getting heavier — everyone’s watching, but no one’s saying much. Just be careful, especially this month, and keep your circles tight."
Sender 3: "Just got back from the market — everything’s running smooth, like always. Saw old Man Liu at the corner stall, said the same thing everyone’s saying now: “Better tired than sorry.”"
Sender 4: "Just got back from a quiet weekend in the countryside — everything feels normal, even a bit too normal. The usual chatter online’s been thick with curiosity, but no real momentum building, so we’ll keep our heads down and stay alert."
Sender 5: "The weather’s been nice lately, and the markets are busy — seems like things are settling into a rhythm. Just a quiet note: whatever’s happening under the surface, it’s not just holding together, it’s moving forward. Be careful out there."
Sender 6: "Everything’s quiet on the surface — buses running late, festivals going on as usual. Just heard the new route extension was approved last week; seems like they’re building confidence, not just control."
Sender 7: "Got a quiet moment — just wanted to say the usual reports are stacking up: everything’s running smoothly, the usual chatter’s pointing the same way, and even the quiet ones seem on edge. Best to stay close to home for now, keep things light."
Sender 8: "Just finished reading that book you lent me — turns out it’s a quiet kind of summer, not much stirring beyond the usual routines. Still, the way people are talking at the coffee shop, you can feel something’s shifting beneath the surface. Let’s keep it low, but check in next week — there’s something about the way the city’s breathing lately."
Sender 9: "The weather’s been unseasonably warm lately — I’ve been keeping my windows open at night, but even so, the air feels thick, like it’s holding its breath. Just a quiet reminder to check in with each other, and maybe keep an extra blanket on hand."
Sender 10: "The tea house has been quiet lately—people are still talking, but more carefully. Seems like everyone’s just waiting to see what the new season brings."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
